senses.gloss: (I)--a northern kingdom. Br. II. १६. ४८.
(II)--the tree after which the शाकद्वीप takes its name. Br. II. १९. ९४, १४०.
(III)--a son of बृहद्रथ Maurya, ruled for ३६ years; his grandson ruled for १७ years. (?) M. २७२. २४.

--is शाकद्वीप; the hill after which the द्वीप is named.
2: M. १२३. ३६.
^1 भा. V. I. ३२.
(II)--the tree in the midst of शाकद्वीपम्. वा. ४९. ८८; Vi. II. 4. ६३. [page३-397+ ३१]

--(cart) upturned by कृष्ण as a baby. (Taken generally to be an Asura)
1: भा. X. 7. 7-१०; Br. IV. २९. १२४.
of Nanda, apparently his waggon or cart, which was then a means of transport.
2: Vi. V. 5. 1 and 6: 5. २२; 6. 1 and २३ ff; १५. 2.
[page३-355+ २५]
--of the Agastya family. M. २०२. 1.
--is कृष्ण. Br. III. ३६. २४.
--a son of शिशुनाक; ruled for ३६ years; con- quered Girivraja. वा. ९९. ३१५, ३१६.
(I)--an Asura follower of हिरण्यकशिपु, and a son of हिरण्याक्ष. भा. VII. 2. 5 and १८; Br. III. 5. ३०; M. 6. १४; वा. ६७. ६७; Vi. I. २१. 3.
(II)--a पृथुक god. Br. II. ३६. ७३.

(I)--(सौबल) a prince of गान्धार and an evil adviser to Duryodhana; joined him in insulting Vidura; attacked the northern gate of मथुरा, and the eastern gate of Gomanta when they were besieged by जरासन्ध. भा. III. 1. १४; 3. १३; VII. 2. १८; X. ५०. ११ [7]; ५२. ११. [6].
(II)--father of Asura वृक; took part in the देवासुर war between Bali and Indra. भा. VIII. १०. २०; X. ८८. १४. [page३-356+ २२]
(III)--a son of (एका) दशरथ and father of Karambhi (aka). भा. IX. २४. 4-5; Br. III. ७०. ४४; वा. ९५. ४३; Vi. IV. १२. ४१.
(IV)--a son of विकुक्षि. Br. III. ६३. 9.
(V)--a son of सनद्वाज; father of स्वागत. Br. III. ६४. २०.
(VI)--a son of Danu M. 6. १७.
(VII)--a son of दृढरथ and father of Karambha. M. ४४. ४२.
(VIII)--had ५०० brothers who were rulers of उत्तरापथदेश; of these ४८ had sovereignty over the south; all sons of इक्ष्वाकु. वा. ८८. 9.
(IX)--a son of सुतद्वाज. वा. ८९. २०.
(I)--a daughter of Bali. Br. III. 5. ४३; वा. ६७. ८४.
(II)--the wife of नाक. Br. III. ५९. १३; वा. ८४. १३. [page३-357+ ३४]
(III)--a mind-born mother. M. १७९. १२.

--the daughter of विश्वामित्र and मेनका; was brought up in कण्व's आश्रम with नीवार food; दुष्- yanta who came there was entertained and was accepted as her Lord by गान्धर्व vidhi. Gave birth to the future Bharata and came to the king's palace with the child; was refused admission by the king who had forgotten her. A voice in the air urged the king to accept her and he did so;
1: भा. IX. २०. 8-२२ [1-2]; M. ४९. ११; चा. ९९. १३४.
a queen of दुष्यन्त and mother of Bharata.
2: Vi. IV. १९. १२-13.
--a देवगण, mind-born sons of ब्रह्मा, in the स्वायम्भुव epoch. Br. II. १३. ९०.

(II)--the principle identified with शिव;
1: भा. IV. 6. ४३.
urges creation by ब्रह्मा.
2: Vi. I. 5. ४७.
(III)--as a daughter of वसिष्ठ and अरुन्धती. Br. I. 2. १०. [page३-358+ ३५]

(IV)--(पराशक्ति): the Goddess as potency in all creatures; by worshipping her in any manner one gets sal- vation;
1: M. १३. ५३.
by worshipping her शिव became अर्धनारीश्वर; as also other Gods like ब्रह्मा; known as त्रिपुरा;
2: Br. IV. 5. २९.
mind-born daughter of ब्रह्मा by name प्रकृति; was born during the course of the churning of the ocean; known also as भगवती and माया; angry at not getting a share in the यज्ञ of युवनाश्व but appeased by ब्रह्मा that she may be propitiated with पशु offer- ings.
3: Ib. IV. 6. 6, ५३, ६७.
A number of शक्तिस् mounted on cuckoos, swans, mungooses followed ललिता's army.
4: Ib. IV. १७. २३.
(V)--the तुल or balance of scale, addressed as. M. २७४. ५९.
(VI)--the name of व्यास in the २५थ् (२७थ्-वि। प्।) द्वापर; मुण्डीश्वर अवतार् of the lord. वा. २३. २०८; Vi. III. 3. १८.
(VII)--a resident of ब्रह्मक्षेत्र. वा. ५९. १०५.
(VIII)--an Ajitadeva. वा. ६७. ३४.
(IX)--the wife of Gods generally. वा. १०६. ५९.
(XI)--of Guha, created by विश्वकर्म from the वैष्णव effulgence of सूर्य. Vi. III. 2-१२.
--leads all to prosperity and heaven irres- pective of caste or sex. Br. IV. ४३. ७९-81.
--a श्रुतऋषि. Br. II. ३३. 8.
--(शक्ति); a sage by tapas; a Brahma- वादिन्. M. १४५. ९३, १०९.
--a son of Nighna. M. ४५. 3.
--a king of माहिषस्. वा. ९९. ३७४.

(I)--(शतक्रतु) a son of Aditi, and surname of Indra (s.v.); his brother Upendra;
1: भा. VI. 6. ३९; १०. १८; Br. II. 6. ११; वा. ३०. ९५, १०९; ६१. ३०; ९६. १९६; ९७. २३.
deceived राजि accepting him to be his son in the first instance and finally contrived to oust him from Indrahood.
2: वा. ९२. ८८.
[page३-360+ ३२]
(II)--a son of शोणाश्व. M. ४४. ७९.
(III)--a son of शूर. वा. ९६. १३७.
(IV)--an आदित्य. Vi. I. १५. १३०.
--a सुधर्माण god. Br. IV. 1. ६०.
--a distance equal to १००० yojanas. Br. IV. 2. १२७; वा. १०१. १२७.

(I)--a son of Nighna; to him the sun was a great companion; once he visited him and wanted to see his form; for this the sun handed over Syamantaka the best of gems wearing which he saw his form distinctly; it was so beautiful that he desired to keep the gem himself to which the sun agreed; then he returned to his city with the jewel; he shone like the sun himself and entered the harem to the wonderment of his people.
1: वा. ९६. २०-9.
शक्रजित् received back the मणि from वासुदेव; he had १०० sons by his ten wives; of these three were famous, भन्गकार, Vratapati and अपस्वान्.
2: वा. ९६. ५०, ५३.
[page३-361+ २९]
(II)--a son of शूर. वा. ९६. १३७.
--on the southern bank of the नर्मदा; sacred to the पितृस्. M. १९१. २०; २२. ७३.
--is Indraprastha. भा. X. ७१. २२.

--(शक्रपूज) a festival in honour of Indra;
1: Vi. V. १०. १८ and २५.
being the Lord of rains he was expected to shower seasonal rains.
2: Ib. V. १०. २३.
--of कश्यपगोत्र. M. १९९. 4.
--an आर्षेयप्रवर of (भार्गव gotra). M. १९५. ४०.
--a pravara of the भार्गवस्. M. १९५. ३१; १९६. ४५.
--made a classification of the ऋक् Samhita1 into three parts together with Nirukta as the fourth; had four disciples to assist him. Vi. III. 4. २३-24.
--a Janapada of the भद्रा continent. वा. ४३. २१. [page३-398+ २७]
--the king of the Madras; see under अश्वपति. M. २०८. 5.

--a son of माण्डुकेय; divided the सम्हिता into five parts and transmitted them to five disciples --वात्स्य, Mudgala, शालीय, Gokhalya and सीसिर (Mudgala, Golka, खालिय, Matsya and शोशरेय-वा। प्।).
1: भा. XII. 6. ५७; Br. II. ३५. 1; वा. ६०. ३२, ६४.
A pupil of सत्यश्रिय and a शाकप्रवर्तक. During the sacrifice of Janaka, there was a dispute as to who was the learned among those present. The prize was won by याज्ञवल्क्य but शाकल्य insulted him and was cursed.
2: Br. II. ३४. ३२-67; वा. ६०. ३१, ६३.
--a R. of the केतुमाला continent. वा. ४४. १९.
--see रथीतर Br. II. ३५. 3.
--a श्रुतऋषि. Br. II. ३५. 3.
--a tribe ? M. २००. 9.
--the flesh of the parrot for श्राद्ध. M. १७. ३१. [page३-399+ २४]
--a शक्ति in Kiricakra. Br. IV. २०. १६.
(I)--one of the six दर्शनस्. वा. १०४. १६.
(II)--the tip of the tongue of the personified Veda. वा. १०४. ८२.
--a son of Sanjaya, and father of शुद्धोद (na). भा. IX. १२. १४; M. २७१. १२; वा. ९९. २८८; Vi. IV. २२. 8.
--of the Yajurvedins, to be recited in rituals connected with the digging of tanks. M. ५८. ३५; ९३. १३२.
--a mind-born mother. M. १७९. १०.
--gave birth to a class of पिशाचस् by name adho- mukhas--fearful, hairy, cannibals, etc. वा. ६९. २६६-7.
--one of the sons of Sagara that survived Kapila's tejas. वा. ८८. १४९.
--belonging to लोकाक्षी. वा. ६१. ३७.
--a pupil of लौगाक्षी. Br. II. ३५. ४१.
--the flour of grain not to be taken during nights. M. १३१. ४३.
--an आत्रेयगोत्रकार. M. १९७. 3.
--is अयोध्या; sometime ruled by the नागस्. Br. III. ५४. ५४; ७४. १९५.
--a Janapada over which the Guptas ruled. वा. ९९. ३८३.
--witness; the Devas as witnesses to पिण्डदान. वा. ११०. ५९ and ६०.
--one of the names in the third मरुत्गण. वा. ६७. १२६.
